title: Adaptive shedder + prefetch guardrail to stabilize token throughput during sudden request surges
creator: Avery Chen
description: Several enterprise customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported sharp drops in sustained tokens/sec and intermittent first-token latency regressions during short-lived request surges. Root cause appears to be a combination of aggressive prefetching (KV/cache pressure) triggering eviction storms and the router queue admitting too many multiplexed sessions simultaneously (worker saturation). We will implement an adaptive shedder that applies short-duration polite rejects for non-critical requests, and a prefetch guardrail that limits concurrent KV prefetches per-worker to prevent cache thrash and kernel fallback churn.
steps_to_reproduce: Synthetic load: 1k concurrent short-chat requests (avg 8 tokens prompt) arriving as a ~20s burst against hosted region us-west2
Use model: open-llm-7b-quant-int8 with default routing and multiplex enabled
Observe tokens/sec drop per worker and increase in kernel fallback rate (see telemetry snippet)
Reproduce also on Dedicated cluster with mixed-priority queues enabled to confirm multi-tenant interaction
telemetry_snippets: Spike window 2026-03-11T15:20Z: global tokens/sec per-GPU fell from 12k to 4k for ~18s
TTFT (first-token) P95 increased from 78ms to 420ms during surge windows
KV prefetch eviction rate increased x5 and kernel selector fallback events rose from 0.2% to 3.6%
Affected: both Hosted and Dedicated pools; Private customer reported similar symptom on 1.21 private agent
mitigation_plan: Short-term (hotfix): deploy router-level temporary admission control that marks non-interactive requests as lower priority and sheds ~30% of them during detected surges
Medium-term: implement per-worker KV prefetch guardrail (max concurrent prefetches = 8, adaptive down to 4 under high eviction)
Deploy adaptive shedder: fast ramp-up to shed low-priority tokens during 2+ second sustained CPU or queue depth increase
Add a server-side circuit that backs off kernel prefetch heuristics when eviction rate > 2% to avoid quant-kernel thrash
Customer communication: notify impacted customers of mitigation and offer dedicated capacity burst buffer while we stabilize
verification_plan: Stage rollout to canary pool (5% of traffic) in hosted; run 3x synthetic surge scenarios and validate tokens/sec and TTFT revert to baseline
Run Dedicated acceptance: apply to a non-production dedicated cluster, run customer-like mixed-priority workload, verify no regression in high-priority latency
Add regression test to CI that replays a recorded surge trace and asserts tokens/sec drop < 20% and TTFT P95 < 200ms
Monitor for 24h post-rollout with automated alerts if KV eviction rate > baseline + 0.5%
